title: Aurora performance annotator: per-model/per-route comparative panels
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable panel for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route performance trade-offs for engineers and platform owners. The "Aurora" panel combines side-by-side comparative cards for:
- Latency distributions (P50/P90/P95/P99 ribbons + percentile bands)
- Throughput & concurrency timeline (requests/sec, active workers)
- Token flow waterfall (prefix vs generated token split, KV cache hits shown as annotations)
- Cost overlay (estimated token cost per time bucket and per-request cost breakdown)

Key UX requirements: compact summary row for high-level SLAs, expandable microview for trace-level inspection, and quick-toggle to align time windows between models/routes for fair comparison. Support lightweight in-console annotations (e.g., deploys, canary rollouts, model swaps) displayed as vertical markers.

Chart/spec decisions (summary):
- Latency chart: stacked percentile ribbons using area+line combo; series: P50/P90/P95/P99; aggregation window 1m for <2h ranges, 5m for >2h; baseline smoothing = 0.2.
- Throughput chart: step-line for rps, bar for concurrency; include moving-avg (60s) toggle.
- Token waterfall: waterfall segmented by token type (prompt, system, gen) with KV cache-hit flag per token; provide per-request hover with token counts and estimated cost.
- Cost overlay: optional translucent layer on top of time series; currency + normalized unit (tokens/request) and 95th percentile cost annotation.

Interactions:
- Sync controls: "Align by time" and "Align by token-length" to rescale x-axis for fair comparison.
- Drill-down: click percentile ribbon to open trace sampler listing top-10 slow requests for that bucket.
- Inline rollout inspector: toggle a rollout layer to see canary vs primary cohorts and costs per cohort.

Accessibility & perf constraints: colorblind-friendly palettes, high contrast mode, and fallback to prerendered sparkline images for very large datasets. Prefer Canvas rendering for waterfall and ribbons to preserve interactivity at high cardinality.

Deliverables: final Figma frames (compact + expanded), JSON chart spec for each visualization (series, transforms, colors, tooltip schema), prototype link and implementation notes for frontend (canvas switch, decimation strategy).
